title: Choose a model
description: Find a model family, a local runtime, and the formats that connect them.
question: What will power your agent?
guide: Model families, weight formats and inference runtimes solve different parts of this task. Compare your tool-calling and structured-output needs against the exact model and backend you plan to use.
caveat: A runtime's license does not cover model weights. Hardware support and tool-calling behavior vary by model and backend.

title: Connect tools & data
description: Give an agent useful actions, typed interfaces, and access to the outside world.
question: What can your agent actually do?
guide: Start with a framework's tool APIs, then consider protocols, connectors and browser automation. An interface format and a working implementation are different kinds of building block.
caveat: A connected tool still needs application-level permissions and error handling. Browser automation does not supply a sandbox.

title: Give it memory
description: Keep useful context across steps, sessions, and changes in the world.
question: What should your agent remember?
guide: Distinguish run checkpoints, conversation history, semantic memories and temporal knowledge graphs. These approaches have different storage, retrieval and lifecycle requirements.
caveat: Memory retrieval needs workload-specific evaluation. Graph ingestion adds database and model requirements; smaller models can produce invalid structured output.

title: Run code safely
description: Set execution boundaries, control permissions, and establish identities.
question: Where are the boundaries?
guide: Sandboxes, workload identity and policy engines cover different boundaries. Match the isolation mechanism to the code and resources your agent can reach.
caveat: MicroVMs are an infrastructure primitive. Host configuration, network policy and workload lifecycle remain integration responsibilities.

title: Keep work running
description: Coordinate steps, pause for a human, and recover when execution fails.
question: Can a run survive the unexpected?
guide: Separate the agent loop from durable execution. Frameworks help decide what happens next; durable runtimes record progress and recover work after interruptions.
caveat: Persistence does not make external side effects exactly-once. Durable workflows need correct replay and idempotency design.

title: Evaluate & observe
description: Inspect traces, test behavior, and track whether changes help.
question: How will you know it works?
guide: Combine offline evaluations with traces from real runs. Observability explains behavior; test cases and assertions measure the outcomes you actually care about.
caveat: Passing an evaluation suite establishes results on those cases. It does not demonstrate reliability on every future task.

title: Serve & deploy
description: Serve inference, schedule compute, and operate the supporting stack.
question: What does it take to operate?
guide: Inference servers, schedulers and interconnect specifications occupy different levels. Start with serving requirements before exploring cluster and hardware infrastructure.
caveat: A serving API does not establish throughput for your workload. Validate the selected model, hardware backend and memory requirements.
